issues.body:
`crates/sparq-py/src/lib.rs:46` is `#![cfg_attr(not(feature = "arrow"), forbid(unsafe_code))]`. That is detector criterion (c) — "cfg(not(feature = F)) or F under any not() anywhere in the crate". `classify_leg(crates/sparq-py, ['arrow'])` returns:

  LegClassification(sensitive=True, reasons=["cfg(not(... feature='arrow' ...)) in .../sparq-py/src/lib.rs"])

The leg added here carries `tier: "check"` with NO `tier-reason:`, which is exactly `cmd_enforce` invariant (1). Running the real `load_fragments()` (169 legs loaded) plus `cmd_enforce`:

  VIOLATION(1) leg 'sparq-py (arrow — Graph.query_arrow -> pyarrow.Table export)': declared tier:check but detector says sensitive ... Add a tier-reason: override or promote the leg back to tier:test.
  1 enforcement violation(s) found.  exit 1

This is the step at .github/workflows/feature-matrix.yml:336 ("Enforce tier ratchet + sq-vya1 guard"). Per the workflow's own error text at :445, that job failing means NO `opt-in *` legs are spawned at all, so every required opt-in check goes MISSING — the gate cannot pass.

I could not run `--enforce` directly (PyYAML is absent in this environment and there is no pip), so I substituted a minimal loader for these flat fragment files; it loaded 169 legs, matching the count round 1 reported, and the classification call itself is unaffected by the stub.

This is not merely a mechanical miss. research/feature-matrix-pyramid.md is internally inconsistent about this leg: §2.1's class table (line 147) types sparq-py (arrow) as **c-only** — sensitive by criterion (c) — while line 192 lists it as the "Clear (1)" demotion candidate. The enforcer is the authority and it says no. I confirmed the old (pre-PR) sanitizer also extracted `not(feature = "arrow")` from this file, so arrow was never demotable under either sanitizer; round 1 left it undemoted, and adding it here is a new CI-breaking change.
issues.fix_hint: Either (a) drop the `tier: "check"` line from the sparq-py arrow leg and correct research/feature-matrix-pyramid.md line 192 / §9's "floor of 1 leg" claim, since the c-only classification at line 147 means there is no clear demotion candidate at all; or (b) if the demotion is genuinely wanted, add a reviewed `tier-reason:` on the leg justifying why the `cfg_attr(not(feature = "arrow"), forbid(unsafe_code))` brace is safe to leave uncompiled per-PR — noting that this attribute is a SAFETY lint guard (it is what enforces that the lean, non-arrow wheel contains zero unsafe code), so demoting it removes per-PR verification that the unsafe-code forbid still holds. Whichever path, run `python3 scripts/feature-matrix-tiers.py --enforce` locally and confirm exit 0 before pushing.
issues.title: arrow demotion violates the tier ratchet (criterion c) — `--enforce` exits 1, reding the required gating job

issues.body:
`_RAW_STRLIT_MASK_RE = (?<![A-Za-z0-9_])(?:br|r)(?P<hashes>#{0,255})"[\s\S]*?"(?P=hashes)` guards only against an identifier prefix. It does not exclude a preceding `"`, `\`, or `'`, so an `r` that is the LAST character of an ordinary string literal — or the `r` of the `\r` escape — is read as a raw-string opener with zero hashes, and `[\s\S]*?` then consumes everything up to the next `"` anywhere in the file. Because raw masking runs BEFORE the regular-literal mask, nothing corrects this.

Minimal reproduction (run against the PR head):

  content = 'let sep = "\\r";\n#[cfg(not(feature = "quoted-triples"))]\nfn materialize_default() {}\n'
  _sanitize_for_cfg_scan(content) ->
    let sep = "\\___
    _____________________quoted-triples"))]
    fn materialize_default() {}
  _extract_cfg_expressions(content) -> []

The live `#[cfg(not(feature = "quoted-triples"))]` is gone. Both new invariants still hold (len preserved, newline count preserved), so the added assertions do not catch it — this is the same fail-open class round 1 blocked on, reached through a different door.

Scanning all 629 crates/*/src/**/*.rs files, this regex produces 86 spurious matches swallowing 13,644 bytes of live Rust. Largest spans: sparq-mpc/src/join.rs:1458 (2,964 bytes), sparq-engine-serialize/src/serialize.rs:147 (1,885) and :3969 (844), sparq-engine/src/window.rs:731 (766). Triggers are ordinary code such as `'\r' => out.push_str("\\r")` (26 files) and string lists containing a bare `"r"`.

On today's tree this costs only one duplicate `test` expression in sparq-server/src/http.rs and flips no leg's sensitivity, hence major not blocker. But the module docstring at line 9 states the core invariant as "A detector bug degrades to 'keep the full leg', never to a silent demotion", and this is a silent erasure in the demotion direction — the property the whole ratchet rests on.
issues.title: New raw-string mask treats `"\r"` / `"...r"` as a raw-string opener, swallowing live source and erasing cfg attributes (fail-OPEN)

issues.body:
The fixture is four clean, well-formed cfg attributes with perfectly balanced quotes. I ran it through a reconstruction of the pre-PR `_sanitize_for_cfg_scan` (strings masked first with the newline-spanning `b?"[^"\\]*(?:\\.[^"\\]*)*"`, comments blanked second) and got:

  OLD: ['all(test, feature = "window-origin")', 'all(test, not(feature = "window-origin"))', 'feature = "quoted-triples"', 'not(feature = "quoted-triples")']
  NEW: identical

So the test would have gone green before the fix and cannot fail on the defect it is named for. The name claims it exercises "cfgs from rsp and reason sources", but the fixture contains none of the material that actually broke those files — the newline-spanning decoy quote. It reads as regression coverage while providing none.

The two sibling tests added alongside it (`test_sanitizer_preserves_lines_and_live_cfg_after_comment_quote` and `test_multiline_raw_string_decoy_preserves_live_cfg`) ARE non-vacuous and do go red against the old sanitizer — the finding is scoped to this third test only.
issues.fix_hint: Either delete it as redundant, or make it non-vacuous by embedding the actual trigger — an unbalanced quote in a doc comment or a multi-line literal ahead of the cfg braces — so it fails against the old sanitizer. Better still, drive it from the real files (read crates/sparq-rsp/src/rspql.rs and crates/sparq-reason/src/incremental.rs when present, skip otherwise) and assert the extracted counts, which pins the regression to the sources that actually regressed.
issues.title: `test_regression_cfgs_from_rsp_and_reason_sources` is vacuous — it passes unchanged against the pre-fix sanitizer

issues.body:
The rewritten docstring says pass 2 will "Mask regular and raw string literal contents with underscores" and that "Newline characters are retained in multiline raw strings". In fact `_STRLIT_MASK_RE` now excludes `\r` and `\n` from its character classes, so an ordinary Rust string literal spanning several physical lines matches nothing and its contents are scanned as live code. The deleted comment block was more honest — it at least documented the raw-string carve-out it had.

This direction is safe (an unmasked decoy yields a false POSITIVE, so the leg stays SENSITIVE and the full leg is kept, which is the fail-closed direction), so it is not a correctness defect. But a future reader will reasonably assume literals are masked and may build on that. `/* ... */` block comments are likewise unhandled by either pass and are not mentioned anywhere.
issues.fix_hint: State the limits explicitly in the docstring: ordinary literals are masked only within a single physical line (multi-line ordinary literals are deliberately left live, which fails closed); raw literals are masked across lines; `/* ... */` block comments are not handled. If the scanner rewrite suggested for the raw-string issue lands, all three carve-outs disappear and the docstring can simply describe the state machine instead.
issues.title: Docstring overstates coverage: multi-line ordinary string literals are now not masked at all, and block comments never were

issues.body:
research/feature-matrix-pyramid.md line 352 specifies sq-s5dvo as "per-test-body audit of the 9 b-coloc legs (§2.1), then annotate only audit-cleared legs (+ sparq-py `arrow`) `tier: check`; mutation demo + before/after counts", and line 389 requires "the measured before/after leg counts from the flip PR as a dated" record. This round carries none of them — the diff is one fragment line plus the detector fix.

Round 1 raised this as part of the scope finding. The scope problem itself is genuinely resolved (19 legs down to 1), so I have dropped the severity, but the recording obligation is unchanged and the design record still asserts a "floor (certain): 1 leg demoted" at line 365 that the ratchet contradicts.

Separately, the design record contemplates the outcome where the audit clears nothing: line 358 records "sparq-py `arrow`" as a valid terminal outcome. Given the criterion-(c) classification, the honest terminal outcome may now be zero legs demoted — which is itself a result worth recording rather than a failure.
issues.fix_hint: Update research/feature-matrix-pyramid.md in this PR with a dated entry giving the before/after demoted-leg count, the per-test-body audit result for whatever legs are demoted (or an explicit "audit cleared nothing" if arrow is dropped per the blocker), and the mutation demo showing the ratchet goes red when a feature-gated test is added under a demoted feature. Reconcile the §2.1 line 147 c-only classification with the line 192 "Clear (1)" claim and the line 365 floor while you are there.
issues.title: Bead deliverables still absent: no audit record, no mutation demo, no before/after leg counts

verdict.summary:
Round 2 narrows the flip dramatically and fixes the reported root cause, but introduces a NEW blocker that reds a required gating job.

Resolved vs round 1: the 19-leg demotion is gone (only sparq-py `arrow` remains), so the scope-overrun, ~246-lost-tests, b-module and security-demotion findings no longer apply. The sanitizer is now genuinely line-preserving: rspql.rs stays 884 lines (was 884->461) and incremental.rs 3272 (was 3272->446); the detector now sees 5 window-origin and 11 quoted-triples cfg expressions where it previously saw zero.

New blocker: the one demotion this PR adds hard-fails the ratchet. `crates/sparq-py/src/lib.rs:46` carries `#![cfg_attr(not(feature = "arrow"), forbid(unsafe_code))]` — detector criterion (c). `classify_leg` returns sensitive=True, the fragment has no `tier-reason:`, so `cmd_enforce` emits VIOLATION(1) and exits 1. I ran the real `load_fragments()` (169 legs) with a stub yaml loader and reproduced it verbatim. This is the gating step at .github/workflows/feature-matrix.yml:336, whose failure suppresses every `opt-in *` leg. The OLD sanitizer also saw this cfg_attr, so arrow was never demotable.

New major: the added `_RAW_STRLIT_MASK_RE` re-opens the fail-open hole. `(?:br|r)#*"[\s\S]*?"` with a lookbehind that only excludes [A-Za-z0-9_] treats `"\r"` and `"...r"` as raw-string openers. Minimal repro: `let sep = "\r";` followed by `#[cfg(not(feature = "quoted-triples"))]` yields `_extract_cfg_expressions() == []` — the live attribute is erased. Across crates/*/src this fires at 86 sites swallowing 13,644 bytes of live Rust (largest single span 2,964 bytes in sparq-mpc/src/join.rs:1458). It costs no leg reclassification today, but it violates the documented core invariant that a detector bug degrades to "keep the full leg, never a silent demotion".

Also: one of the three new tests is vacuous, and the bead's audit/mutation-demo/before-after deliverables are still absent.
